hpx.native.application.admission.title: Command admission and transaction scope
hpx.native.application.admission.description: Frozen command validation, original digest and current writer transaction scope in existing Workspace methods. Current authority precedes protected replay; session authentication/unlock occur outside this responsibility.

hpx.native.application.replay.title: Original operation and receipt reconciliation
hpx.native.application.replay.description: Compare exact operation/digest and recheck current result authority; authorized exact retry returns the original receipt before mutable generation preconditions. This is local replay, not exactly-once external delivery.

hpx.native.application.dispatch.title: Feature operation coordination
hpx.native.application.dispatch.description: Existing Command match delegates to co-located document/branch, Fork/synthesis, checkpoint/reference, assertion and comment helpers. Helpers invoke pure rules and stage effects in the same transaction; no new dispatcher module or service is selected.

hpx.native.application.publication.title: Atomic outcome and receipt publication
hpx.native.application.publication.description: One existing transaction binds the staged feature result and original receipt before COMMIT. Draft acknowledgement is not an immutable text Commit; Commit/history construction remains feature-specific. No second transaction manager is introduced.

hpx.native.application.reads.title: Protected read entry points
hpx.native.application.reads.description: Logical group of existing protected Workspace read methods; runtime calls these directly rather than through execute. Current scope and bounded consistent views remain method-specific. No shared read facade or general navigation engine exists.

hpx.native.storage.access.title: Workspace creation and supported opening
hpx.native.storage.access.description: Create-only local workspace and explicit existing-file opening; normal readers accept schemas1/2, authenticate catalog and configure bundled SQLite WAL/FULL. Passphrase is default; no implicit migration, creation on open, keychain enrollment or schema3 activation.

hpx.native.storage.records.title: Versioned record and envelope boundary
hpx.native.storage.records.description: Adapter-owned strict record version/kind decoding and typed identity/snapshot codecs. Cipher builds expected workspace/kind/identity/generation binding and invokes crypto; domain records remain dependency-free. Crypto context authentication is not current authorization.

hpx.native.storage.record_store.title: Immutable records and mutable heads
hpx.native.storage.record_store.description: Existing SQLite object/slot operations, immutable insertion and expected-generation updates participate in caller-owned transactions. Encrypted record bodies coexist with visible bootstrap/structural metadata and WAL/SHM. No database server or independent storage process.

hpx.native.crypto.material.title: Managed key lifetime and entropy
hpx.native.crypto.material.description: OS-random key/nonce/salt generation and zeroizing managed secret buffers. No fallback entropy, raw data-key export, complete hostile-host erasure guarantee or TLS-key management.

hpx.native.crypto.envelopes.title: Context-bound record encryption
hpx.native.crypto.envelopes.description: Bounded authenticated object envelopes using caller-supplied expected context; plaintext is returned only after authentication. Purpose/binding are not permission grants. No record decoding, file/network IO or policy decisions.

hpx.native.crypto.wrapping.title: Passphrase and device-secret wrapping
hpx.native.crypto.wrapping.description: Wrap/unlock the same workspace data key against expected workspace/epoch, with exact supported framing/profile guards before derivation. Retained old wrappers remain usable; no implicit rotation, revocation or new custody mode.

hpx.native.crypto.derivation.title: Bounded password derivation
hpx.native.crypto.derivation.description: Fixed Argon2id profile, checked allocation and zeroizing KDF backing memory; caller passphrase allocations/concurrent aggregate work are outside this primitive. No password storage or provider lookup.

hpx.native.crypto.addressing.title: Ciphertext address calculation
hpx.native.crypto.addressing.description: SHA256 of complete encrypted bytes, separate from logical identity and authentication. Existing tests consume this helper; no production storage consumer was found. SQLite object identity must not be depicted as ciphertext-hash addressing.

hpx.native.keychain.lifecycle.title: Explicit enrollment and removal
hpx.native.keychain.lifecycle.description: Enrollment/removal require explicit unlocked owner scope; status can read bootstrap enrollment while locked without accessing native credentials. Preserve passphrase wrapper; schema1 upgrade first verifies backup. Create native item before wrapper commit; remove wrapper before native deletion. No startup enrollment or general key revocation.

hpx.native.keychain.unlock.title: Workspace-bound alternative unlock
hpx.native.keychain.unlock.description: Explicitly load the selected workspace device secret and unlock/verify the same data key; authenticate catalog through supported workspace opening. No browser keys, human passphrase storage or session/resource authorization grant.

hpx.native.keychain.provider.title: Native scoped credential operations
hpx.native.keychain.provider.description: Actual native provider boundary: inert capability query, create-only workspace-scoped item, load and expected-secret checked removal. macOS file-keychain implementation; other targets return unavailable. No file/env/cloud fallback or atomic compare-and-delete guarantee.

hpx.native.keychain.backup.title: Verified pre-upgrade recovery copy
hpx.native.keychain.backup.description: Consistent schema1 encrypted SQLite backup, restrictive file/directory permissions, fingerprint verification and source recheck before explicit upgrade. No portable/remote backup, general repair or backup on ordinary open.

hpx.native.keychain.cleanup.title: Failed native cleanup and retry state
hpx.native.keychain.cleanup.description: A failed scoped item removal retains the expected secret only in the unlocked process for retry. Lock/exit drops it; a crash orphan is not silently overwritten/deleted. No durable cleanup daemon or erasure guarantee.

c3_application.title: C3 / Application coordination
c3_application.scope: Logical responsibilities in current co-located Workspace methods, not a new application crate/services. Current authority before protected replay; draft ACK differs from Commit. Direct protected reads bypass command execution. Solid arrows are evidenced dependencies, with returns implicit, not a sequence or an adopted V3 refactor.

c3_workspace_persistence.title: C3 / Workspace persistence
c3_workspace_persistence.scope: Supported opening, adapter-owned representation and embedded SQLite state in the same Rust executable. Logical grouping is proposed, not new storage services. Encrypted bodies do not hide all structural metadata. WAL/transactions do not establish authenticated provenance, arbitrary closure, rollback detection or federation. Wider repair/temporal upgrade remain separate.

c3_crypto.title: C3 / Cryptographic adapter
c3_crypto.scope: In-memory responsibility decomposition of the existing crypto crate. Solid arrows are calls/dependencies; dotted arrows are managed-secret data dependencies. Current authority and expected context come from callers. Key/nonce entropy is OS-backed; no filesystem/network policy or TLS key lifecycle is implemented here. Address utility is not wired into production SQLite addressing.

c3_keychain.title: C3 / Keychain adapter
c3_keychain.scope: Explicit ADR014 lifecycle, native provider, verified upgrade backup and cleanup ordering. Logical parts share existing files, not new processes. macOS support is bounded; passphrase recovery retained. Enrollment/removal are not startup actions or revocation/erasure guarantees. Arrows describe dependencies, not a full sequence. No credential/state operation runs for this model.

c3_integrations.title: C3 / Integration adapters (proposal)
c3_integrations.scope: Specification-backed proposal only: six existing planned roles, no native provider implementation or selected wire/packaging protocols. Dashed links are planned contracts; current browser-only exact Markdown download is separate. Disclosure/execution policy must be rechecked, and non-trusted plaintext egress remains denied by required core policy. External jobs are not atomic local transactions; no exactly-once remote-write guarantee.
